items.title: Trump may have lost a 'game of chicken' with Iran, which exposed a red line
items.description: It appears that by sparking Iran's escalating strikes on Qatar, Israel caused a headache for US President Donald Trump. Here's what could have played out behind the scenes.

items.title: Live: Trump gives Iran a 48-hour deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: US President Donald Trump is warning the US will "obliterate" Iran’s power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened within 48 hours. Follow live.

items.title: Australia facing 'crunch time' as oil shortages move up supply chain
items.description: Australia is yet to directly feel the impact of supply shortages caused by the Iran war. But that's set to change in the coming weeks, with oil supply shortages now hitting the country's fuel suppliers in Asia.

items.title: Six fuel ships to Australia cancelled or deferred, though gap has been filled
items.description: Energy Minister Chris Bowen says six fuel tankers that were scheduled to deliver oil to Australia next month were recently cancelled or deferred, out of about 81 ships expected from mid-April to mid-May — assuring however that supply gap has already been largely replaced.

items.title: Live: Narelle downgraded as NT braces for flood, WA enters warning zone
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle has been downgraded to a tropical low as it moves across the Northern Territory towards Western Australia.

items.title: Track Cyclone Narelle live as it crosses the NT
items.description: Track the path of Tropical Cyclone Narelle and see live wind speeds as the system travels across the Northern Territory.

items.title: Labor retains power in South Australia as One Nation surges
items.description: The Labor Party has been re-elected in South Australia, while the Liberal Party's vote has collapsed as One Nation appears to have achieved its best electoral result anywhere in the country in nearly 30 years.

items.title: Ex-FBI director Robert Mueller dies at 81, Trump says he's 'glad he's dead'
items.description: Robert Mueller, the no-nonsense former FBI chief who documented Russia's interference in the 2016 US election and its contacts with Donald Trump's campaign — but opted not to bring criminal charges against a sitting president — dies aged 81.

items.title: WA walks tightrope on fuel supply fears as Middle East war intensifies
items.description: As West Australians feel the effects of skyrocketing fuel amid the Middle East conflict, the government is treading the line between raising the alarm and sensible action, writes Courtney Withers.

items.title: 'Terrible injuries': Surgeon's warning as illegal e-bikes surge in popularity
items.description: Bans on children riding e-mobility devices are being considered by several states, but a frontline surgeon says more must be done to stop "preventable injuries".

items.title: Where Australians are spending their money
items.description: As the cost-of-living crisis intensifies, people from all walks of life are struggling. ABC Your Say asked ordinary Australians how they were making ends meet.

items.title: These two dads say Australia needs to talk about compensating surrogates
items.description: Blind spots in surrogacy laws have been pushing desperate Australians overseas to get a baby, which comes with its own risks. Is it time to change our views on paying for surrogacy?

items.title: Father and son take 1,300km bushwalking 'gap year'
items.description: Daniel Toole has taken a year off work to walk around the world with his 18-year-old, non-verbal son, Ashton, who is living with autism spectrum disorder and Tourette syndrome.

items.title: Matildas endure familiar pain in Asian Cup final, but will the relief ever come?
items.description: The Matildas were despondent after losing the Asian Cup final to Japan for the third time, as the golden generation's shot at a major trophy may have passed.

items.title: Far North Queensland takes stock of cyclone damage as clean-up begins
items.description: As Tropical Cyclone Narelle crosses the Northern Territory, communities in Far North Queensland are counting the cost and cleaning up, hopeful power and reception will be restored soon.

items.title: 'We can't recreate the past': Oxford Street blow as queer venue shuts
items.description: Craig Bell, the owner of Stonewall Hotel, said the decision was "sad and difficult" but "change is constant, and Stonewall’s story is far from over".

items.title: From the salon to the sheds: How Brittnee found her passion in shearing
items.description: These women have found a community in an unlikely place — the male-dominated shearing sheds. From wool-classers to rouseabouts, this is how they play their vital part.

items.title: Give musician Flying Lotus 13 minutes, and he'll blow up your brain
items.description: Ahead of an Australian show, the musician, filmmaker and Brainfeeder label founder talks about discovering a new process for his Big Mama EP.

items.title: It's Sunday and that means quiz time. Let's play, HARD!
items.description: Don't blame your poor performance on a slow-start Sunday. We all know the result would be the same on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday …

items.title: Aussie qualifier stuns former world number one Osaka at Miami Open
items.description: Fresh from her Indian Wells quarterfinal appearance, Talia Gibson causes a boilover with her straight-sets defeat of four-time major winner Naomi Osaka in Miami.

items.title: Kings deny roughing up Cotton in NBL Championship Series opener
items.description: Kings coach Brian Goorjian insists there was "no intent" to deliberately target Bryce Cotton, as his side defeats the 36ers by 44 points in Sydney.

items.title: How 'white supremacist' material was used to hire an army of ICE agents
items.description: The White House faces scrutiny over posts experts describe as "flat out white supremacist" amid calls for oversight after ICE agents left "death cards" in immigrants' cars.

items.title: Preserved footprints show Tasmanian tigers in South Australia 120,000 years ago
items.description: The discovery of ancient footprints shows the carnivorous marsupial once roamed the Eyre Peninsula coastline.

items.title: Does an acid attack in Indonesia signal its democratic unravelling?
items.description: An acid attack that seriously burned an Indonesian human rights campaigner reflects a pattern of authoritarian resurgence, in which any form of confrontational activism is viewed as a threat to the state that must be crushed.

items.title: What is stagflation and what can we do about it?
items.description: As the Iran war dries up oil and gas supplies, should we prepare for stagflation?
